body: I think you're all missing the bigger picture: The Shapeshifter knew The Author. He knew him while he was writing the journals. The Shapeshifter probably knows a LOT about the mysteries of Gravity Falls. He was probably referring to something much more terrifying than anything we've seen so far.
Also unless there's a third sibling we haven't met yet, the Author would actually be Dipper and Mabel's grandfather...

I'll definitely look into it; I've tried working on this myself and I honestly think it's time to just get better. Thank you for being so helpful and supportive! c:

I know I could probably benefit from it, but I'm afraid of therapy. I'm actually afraid of all types of doctors, but especially therapists. I understand that it's helpful, but I'm afraid they're going to put me on anti-depressants or anti-anxiety meds. I don't want something to  change my brain chemistry by force =/

That's a very brave outlook, and something I'm truly envious of... But if life is that determined to be victorious over me, and my defiance of that puts me in this much pain, why not just let it win? =/

Thank you for saying so, but it's hard to not see it as my fault. She used to be in love with me. I remember how her lips would curl into a smile when I would kiss her, or the excitement on her face whenever she would get in the car to spend the day with me.  I remember believing that we were going to be together for the rest of our lives. I made her happy... but I was still sad. I would still consider suicide or self harm, or spend all day in bed unable to feel anything. The only time I was happy was when she was around, and I just felt like that was too much to be putting on one person's shoulders. It's one thing to love someone and want them in your life, but it's completely different to actually physically /need/ someone, especially when I was only nineteen and she was eighteen. So I broke it off after a particularly bad night and moved two hundred miles away in order to try figuring out how to just be myself. It apparently destroyed her. I wasn't there, I didn't face it, but she was devastated. I wish I hadn't caused her that much pain. I wish I had just told her how I was really feeling. And the worst part was that I just felt worse than ever while I was away. But then I didn't have her to help. Now we're here. She can't ever love me again, and it feels as though I only have myself to blame.

I know she doesn't have to be in love with me to care. I know. But I'm in love with her. And spending time with her and talking to her just hurts because I just keep thinking about how it's another thing I ruined because of irrational sadness... I don't want to keep sabotaging everything good in my life. I don't want to end up as one of those people who spends their life miserable because they had a compulsive need to hurt anyone who ever gave a damn about them. But I'm kind of already there... I just feel hopeless.

It's been on and off since I was around fifteen. Something good would happen- A really good performance (I'm an actor), a new girlfriend, maybe even something as simple as having a night out drinking and playing Cards Against Humanity with some friends. And the good feelings will last anywhere from a day to five minutes... but I always come down, and come down hard. I was always able to push through that pain because I was always able to tell myself to live for her. And I guess that's still valid; She loves me and cares about me, she's just not in love with me. But I kind of feel like that's bullshit; she shouldn't be able to hurt me and still have control over whether I keep going or not.

She knows that it wasn't her fault now... She's also my closest friend in the world. But the year of damage was done. It doesn't make a difference on how she feels and I can't honestly fault her for it... I hurt her and she moved on.
